sources.title: Côte d’Ivoire : Grève sur le pétrolier FPSO Espoir, la production à l’arrêt, les travailleurs durcissent le ton
sources.provenance: KOACI, directly opened in French. Page headline and search-result summary report workers stopped work from April 18 and production halted amid labor demands; open page extraction exposed date/headline but little article body.

provisional_leads.assessment: Potential labor-action lead with a specific reported start date; retain as provisional pending corroboration because the article body was not extractable in the open view.
provisional_leads.uncertainty: Details and demands rely on the result summary and headline, not fully accessible article text.

provisional_leads.status: reported by Reuters as having occurred the prior week
provisional_leads.event_date: 2026-05-04 to 2026-05-10 (Reuters only specifies ‘last week’; exact day not established)

sources.title: Ivory Coast will send officials to calm protests by cocoa farmers, source says
sources.excerpt: police tear-gassed dozens of farmers last week as they blocked roads
sources.provenance: Reuters, directly opened; article says protests concerned unpaid cocoa sales and unsold stocks, and local officials would be sent to calm tensions. Reuters attributes some details to a source close to the Cocoa and Coffee Council and farmers/cooperatives.

provisional_leads.assessment: Strong provisional protest lead with road blockade and specific demands over payment for cocoa; exact day and crowd totals remain uncertain.
provisional_leads.uncertainty: Reuters dates action only as ‘last week’; police action is reported but not independently verified here.

provisional_leads.status: reported event; further legal aftermath corroborates date and arrests
provisional_leads.actors: Côte d’Ivoire Maritime Affairs Administration agents; SYNABEPAM union
provisional_leads.publication_date: 2026-06-16 (EU SEE alert; later FIDH follow-up dated 2026-07-24)

sources.title: Crackdown on the Maritime Affairs workers’ strike in Abidjan
sources.excerpt: agents of the Maritime Affairs Administration in Côte d’Ivoire went on strike
sources.provenance: EU SEE/Hivos alert, directly opened, with English and French text; reports demands including a housing allowance and increased sector bonuses, and approximately 34 arrests.

sources.title: Côte d’Ivoire : 31 agent·es des Affaires maritimes condamné·es à un an de prison après avoir exercé leur droit de grève
sources.excerpt: Le 8 juin 2026, 34 grévistes ont été arbitrairement arrêtés
sources.provenance: FIDH, directly opened in French; subsequent legal follow-up confirms date and describes a sit-in outside maritime police headquarters. This page is after Q2; used only to corroborate the June event, not as an in-quarter publication.

provisional_leads.assessment: Well-supported provisional labor mobilization lead; workers protested for benefits and bonuses, followed by arrests and later prosecutions reported by rights organizations.
provisional_leads.uncertainty: Arrest count is approximately 34 initially; the later FIDH headline says 31 were convicted. Treat charges, arrests, convictions, and protest event as distinct facts.
